properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-11, thinking out loud — nothing here is settled and nothing should be quoted back as intent.

HIS IDEA, IN HIS WORDS: "attach some type of additional parameters to each requirement or capability node. something that accounts for the full lifecycle of that requirement/capability. for instance, have fields for: develop-using, development-test-plan, operational-test-plan, production-plan, operational-deployed. there might be other 'dimensions' to a requirement node, but having something at the very beginning of design that already has an agent/user thinking from the get-go how it will eventually be fielded in an operational environment is good to have upfront. many of the things may be unknown-at-this-moment or N/A, but at least something is there to drive the thought process."

⭐ THE GOAL IS THE PROMPT, NOT THE FIELD. Read his last sentence: the value he names is that the question gets ASKED early, and he expects most answers to be empty. That is a statement about when a thought happens, not about where a value is stored — and it is what separates the options below. An option that stores five mostly-empty fields but never asks anything would miss the point entirely; an option that asks all five questions and stores nothing until there is an answer would meet it.

WHAT THE DESIGN ALREADY HOLDS, so a later reader is not re-deciding settled ground. Each of his five axes already has machinery, but scattered and edge-shaped rather than gathered on the node:
- development-test-plan / operational-test-plan — `dec:idea-verification-is-planned-with-the-requirement` is ALREADY OPEN and asks almost exactly this: "should reflow2 guide a project to plan HOW a need will be verified when the need is stated, rather than only asking for a check once something is built?" His two test-plan axes are that question, split into a development arm and an operational arm — which is a V-model distinction that open question does not currently draw.
- operational-deployed — Environment nodes, `deploy_to`, `reconcile_deployment` and `cmp:fielded` already model where something actually runs.
- production-plan / readiness to field — the Readiness layer (TRL/MRL, ReadinessAssessment, GATED_ON with a required `min_level`) already models whether a thing is mature enough to field, and `SCHEDULED_FOR` models when it is due.
- develop-using — nothing obvious models this. It is the one axis with no existing home.
- Requirement already carries a five-state lifecycle (proposed/accepted/deferred/dropped/met) of which THREE ARE UNUSED — recorded in `chg:bl104-derived-completion` as "the requirement lifecycle is 3/5 unused". Any new lifecycle vocabulary has to answer why it would fare better than the one already there and unused.

THE OPTIONS, with what is cheap and what is expensive about each.

A — PROPERTIES ON THE NODE, his literal proposal. Five enum/string fields on Requirement and Capability. Cheapest to build (schema YAML), and the fields are visible in every export and every view, so they nag by existing. EXPENSIVE: BL-198 has just spent this month REMOVING stored defaults — 3,207 of them across 59% of nodes — because a value written by the tool rather than by a person makes `compare_designs` unable to tell a default from a decision. Five fields defaulting to "unknown" on every node is that exact shape, freshly re-introduced. And "N/A" written by an agent is a judgement about scope, which `dec:readiness-is-an-observation-the-threshold-is-the-judgement` says the tool does not get to make on the user's behalf.

B — ASK THE FIVE QUESTIONS, STORE NOTHING UNTIL THERE IS AN ANSWER. A gap detector in the existing detect-and-ask loop that asks, of a requirement, "how will this be developed / checked in development / checked in operations / produced / fielded?" No schema change; nothing is stored until somebody answers, so silence stays silence and never becomes a stored "unknown". Matches the goal he actually stated, since the thought is what he wants triggered. EXPENSIVE: the loop already owes 67 unasked gaps, and five new questions on every requirement would swamp it — this needs a rule about WHICH requirements deserve the questions (and when), or it drowns the thing it is added to.

C — EDGES TO REAL NODES, which is what reflow2 does today. A test plan is a Verification, a production plan is a Release/DesignEpoch, fielding is an Environment. Nothing new at all. CHEAP and already queryable end to end. EXPENSIVE, and this is Anthony's actual complaint: it only ever happens when somebody REMEMBERS to draw the edge, so the thinking never gets prompted at the start — which is the whole thing he is asking for.

D — A SIDE NODE PER AXIS, on the DimensionAssessment pattern that already exists for cross-cutting concerns. Keeps the requirement clean, lets an axis carry its own provenance and date, and extends to "other dimensions" without another schema change each time — which is the extensibility his aside asks about. EXPENSIVE: a node per axis per requirement is a lot of graph for something usually empty, and it is the heaviest of the four.

THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT TO THE WHOLE IDEA, recorded beside it rather than used to kill it: a checklist filled with "unknown-at-this-moment" on every node teaches people to skip it, and then reflow2 holds five more fields nobody reads — the exact failure already measured twice here, in the 3-of-5 unused requirement lifecycle and in the two evidence-quality axes used zero times. Whatever is chosen has to say what READS the answer, because a marker nothing reads is a comment.

NOT DECIDED, and deliberately not ranked. B and C are not exclusive — B could be the prompt that leads to C's edges, which would need no new vocabulary at all.
properties.name: OPEN — should a Requirement/Capability carry lifecycle dimensions from the moment it is written, so fielding is thought about at the start?
properties.rationale: Anthony's, 2026-08-11: "having something at the very beginning of design that already has an agent/user thinking from the get-go how it will eventually be fielded in an operational environment is good to have upfront." The design's V-model has both arms and no rungs, and this is a proposal for rungs stated at the top of the left arm — which is why it is worth recording even though four of the five axes already have scattered machinery.
